A0.reason: Active-core count checked PER REGIME against A0's criterion (interleaved: active == min(grid, total_blocks)) on this 11x10=110 grid: square 256 blocks -> 110 cores; wide_short 32 blocks -> 32 cores; tall_narrow 64 -> 64; l1_to_l1 64 -> 64; smallest 1 -> 1. All match. No bandwidth-knee cap: tilize's reader is transaction-rate bound and master.md A0 records the cap measuring ~2.4x SLOWER on this very op, so the full grid is used. REFINEMENT 1 (A1): use_multicore=True is now IN SUPPORTED, so this lever is the SHIPPED default path rather than a wired-but-unclaimed parameter value (Phase 0 shipped the 1-core value). Re-measured this phase; the off-arm is the same `levers=dict(multicore=0)` bench arm. Core count asserted, never inferred: test_tilize_debug.py::test_multicore_fills_the_grid_on_wide_short and ::test_a1_wide_short_golden_cell_fills_the_grid.

measured.note: Refinement 1 re-measure, per-regime off/on: square 7.544x, wide_short 6.092x, tall_narrow 16.809x, l1_to_l1[1,1,512,2048] 11.520x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.000x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.004x. The two 1-block shapes are 1.00x BY CONSTRUCTION (one block cannot be spread), which is master.md B0's requirement satisfied rather than a miss.

A1.reason: split_work_to_cores(..., row_wise=True) AND grid_to_cores(..., row_wise=True) — the same flag on both calls, or the runtime-arg assignment order silently mismatches the split's group order (op_design risk 18). Pays on the many-core regimes; inside the ~2-3% noise band on the DRAM-saturated square and on the 1-core smallest shapes, which is expected — with one core there is no core line to orient.

measured.note: per-regime off/on: square 0.996x, wide_short 1.109x, tall_narrow 1.022x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 0.978x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.024x

A2.reason: Sharded calls launch on the shard's OWN cores via get_optimal_worker_cores_for_sharded_tensor (shard_grid_cores in the program descriptor) — core k holds shard k — instead of re-spreading the linear block space with split_work_to_cores. A2 and C14 are one edit on this op (the pinned cores are what makes the CB alias legal), so they share the force_streamed off-arm: with it on, the same call re-spreads across the grid AND re-fetches the shard over the NoC. per-regime off/on: sharded_big (64 cores, 1 block each) 10.144x, sharded_small (4 cores, 4 blocks each) 2.754x — it pays on the smallest sharded regime too, which is B0's requirement.

measured.note: same-spec HEIGHT-sharded L1->L1, shard (32,2048) on an 8x8 grid; off-arm = levers=dict(force_streamed=1). Second regime measured on sharded_small [1,1,512,64] shard (128,64) on 4 cores: 851.7 vs 2345.3 ns.

A3.followup: Map the linear block index -> a bank-adjacent core (reader next to the DRAM bank it reads) instead of the plain row-wise line, and re-measure the square. The block->core mapping is already a host-side function, so this is a placement change only.
A3.reason: The square measures 376 GB/s of DRAM traffic against a ~448 GB/s theoretical peak (84%), and the tech report's placed/adjacent recipe reaches ~92% — so ~9% is the size of what bank-adjacency (with B10's per-reader VCs) could still buy. Deferred rather than refuted because interleaved round-robin pages touch every bank, which weakens the adjacency argument for THIS memory layout: it needs measuring, not asserting.

A4.followup: Revisit only if a profile ever shows the tail-column-block cores idling: specialize them into their own kernel instead of carrying (n_full, n_tail) as runtime args.
A4.reason: The two-group split already carries the remainder in a runtime arg, and the tail column-block is a second COMPILE-TIME instantiation of the same compute kernel (WT_TAIL), so there is no cliff kernel to skip and no idle core to reclaim. Predicted 0 rather than structurally-impossible because a cliff kernel IS buildable — it just has nothing to win here.

B0.reason: The discipline itself: every per-core-overhead lever in this ledger (B5, B7, and B9) is counterfactualed on the smallest regime the op runs in as well as on the square, so a lever that pays at several blocks/core cannot silently regress the 1-block case. All three DID pay on the smallest shape (B7 6.03x, B5 1.027x, B9 1.045x), so none needed a work-per-core gate. The measurement below is B7's smallest-regime arm, the strongest instance. Measured on [1,1,32,32] — the smallest shape the Phase-0 op can RUN (1 core, 1 block, 1 tile). feature_spec.INPUTS' global smallest is [1,1,30,32], but that is a pad_mode="auto" cell which Phase 0 refuses (padding is refinement P1), and [1,1,32,32] is its tile-aligned counterpart with the identical per-core geometry (nt_h=1, Wt=1, one block). FOLLOW-UP for P1: re-run these arms on [1,1,30,32] once the padded reader exists, since the pad fill adds per-block L1 stores that this shape does not carry.

measured.note: Measured on [1,1,32,32] — the smallest shape the Phase-0 op can RUN (1 core, 1 block, 1 tile). feature_spec.INPUTS' global smallest is [1,1,30,32], but that is a pad_mode="auto" cell which Phase 0 refuses (padding is refinement P1), and [1,1,32,32] is its tile-aligned counterpart with the identical per-core geometry (nt_h=1, Wt=1, one block). B5.reason: The writer writes each output tile as ONE whole-page noc_async_write instead of four face-sized writes. Small but consistent, and it pays on the smallest regime too, which is B0's requirement for a per-core-overhead lever. per-regime off/on: square 1.026x, wide_short 1.061x, tall_narrow 1.031x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.027x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.098x

measured.note: Measured on [1,1,32,32] — the smallest shape the Phase-0 op can RUN (1 core, 1 block, 1 tile). feature_spec.INPUTS' global smallest is [1,1,30,32], but that is a pad_mode="auto" cell which Phase 0 refuses (padding is refinement P1), and [1,1,32,32] is its tile-aligned counterpart with the identical per-core geometry (nt_h=1, Wt=1, one block). FOLLOW-UP for P1: re-run these arms on [1,1,30,32] once the padded reader exists, since the pad fill adds per-block L1 stores that this shape does not carry.

B6.reason: TARGET_READ_BYTES is a BYTE target (so every dtype lands on the same sweet spot) and the sweep MOVED it: 512 B — the Wormhole one-packet value op_design.md specified — is wrong on this Blackhole part, where NOC_MAX_BURST_SIZE is 256 words x 64 B = 16 KB so the one-packet argument does not bind at 512 B. Square sweep: 128 B 151.3us | 256 B 86.5us | 512 B 55.3us | 1024 B 44.6us | 2048 B 44.7us | 4096 B 47.2us. wide_short: 512 B 1.060x, 2048 B 1.090x, 4096 B 1.280x vs 1024 B. tall_narrow and both smallest shapes are unaffected (WT_BLOCK = min(Wt, ...) clamps). Default moved 512 -> 1024: 1.24x on the square, 1.06x on wide_short, no regression in any regime.

measured.note: off_ns is the 512 B arm (op_design's specified value); full sweep in the reason

B7.reason: One noc_async_read_barrier per BLOCK (tile_h reads in flight), which is exactly what dataflow_kernel_lib::read_sticks_for_tilize<TILE> does; the off-arm barriers every transaction. The largest transaction-shape lever in the op, and it pays in EVERY regime — most of all on the smallest one — so no work-per-core gate is needed. per-regime off/on: square 1.242x, wide_short 2.242x, tall_narrow 2.465x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 6.025x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 6.132x

measured.note: Measured on [1,1,32,32] — the smallest shape the Phase-0 op can RUN (1 core, 1 block, 1 tile). feature_spec.INPUTS' global smallest is [1,1,30,32], but that is a pad_mode="auto" cell which Phase 0 refuses (padding is refinement P1), and [1,1,32,32] is its tile-aligned counterpart with the identical per-core geometry (nt_h=1, Wt=1, one block). FOLLOW-UP for P1: re-run these arms on [1,1,30,32] once the padded reader exists, since the pad fill adds per-block L1 stores that this shape does not carry.

B8.followup: Add a `trid` knob to the reader (tag each block's reads with a transaction id, barrier on the PREVIOUS id) and measure on the square — the only benched shape with several blocks per core (256 blocks / 110 cores). Compare against split_reader, the other way to keep reads in flight.
B8.reason: Structurally invisible on the 1-block-per-core shapes (wide_short at the current WT_BLOCK, tall_narrow, both smallest), which per master.md B8 is a BENCH property and not evidence the lever fails. The square is where it could show: its ablation says read and write are co-binding with compute fully hidden, so more outstanding reads is the plausible next lever. Deferred on scope, not refuted.

B9.reason: Reader on NCRISC/NoC0 (ReaderConfigDescriptor) and writer on BRISC/NoC1 (WriterConfigDescriptor); the off-arm swaps the two configs so the read stream runs on the writer's NoC. Pays in every regime, including the smallest, and is the second-largest lever on the square. per-regime off/on: square 1.273x, wide_short 1.864x, tall_narrow 1.118x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.045x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.062x

measured.note: per-regime off/on: square 1.273x, wide_short 1.864x, tall_narrow 1.118x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.045x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.062x

B10.followup: Assign per-reader VCs (the vc/use_vc params on the dataflow read/write API) so readers sharing a route stop serializing FCFS; measure on the square and wide_short. Pair it with A3 (bank-adjacent placement) — the tech report applies them together.
B10.reason: Same headroom as A3 (the square sits at 84% of DRAM peak vs the ~92% placed+VC recipe); the two levers are not additive, so 9% is the JOINT estimate, not 9% each. Per B0 it can regress the smallest regime, so it would ship gated on work-per-core.

B11.reason: There is no misalignment for the lever to fix at any element width the current or next refinement reaches: every read is WT_BLOCK*32*elem bytes and every write is a whole tile page, both multiples of this part's DRAM alignment unit for 2 B and 4 B dtypes at every Wt (pinned by the named test). ONE exception is recorded rather than hidden: a 1-byte dtype with Wt == 1 yields a 32 B read, below the 64 B unit — out of SUPPORTED at Phase 0, explicitly owned by refinement A5b's alignment-aware narrow-stick reader, and pinned by test_b11_uint8_narrow_stick_is_the_known_alignment_gap so it cannot ship silently.

B12.reason: tilize's map is a BIJECTION on byte positions and its single input operand varies along BOTH split axes, so no core reads a byte another core reads and there is no fan-out to multicast. Pinned by asserting the program declares no semaphores (a multicast handshake needs them) and that the per-core block ranges tile the block space exactly once.

B13.followup: Add a `set_state` knob to the reader (configure the command buffer once, then issue same-shape reads with with_state) and SWEEP it across target_read_bytes — a prior run found this lever inverts with transaction size (+19.9% at 512 B, 0.950-0.978 at <=128 B), so one measurement would decide it wrongly. Per B0, measure the smallest regime too.
B13.reason: Buildable here: every read in a block has the same size and the same L1 stride; only the source page changes. Deliberately NOT closed by the argument that interleaved DRAM puts consecutive sticks on different banks — that exact (correct) premise is what a prior run used to reject the lever, and measurement then found it wins below 128 B. It owes a number; deferred on scope.

C14.reason: FIRST degree taken: both CBs are aliased onto the resident L1 shards with ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor, so the reader issues no NoC read (it only arms the CB), tilize packs straight into the output shard, and the writer only drains it — zero bytes moved on either side. Structurally verified, not inferred: test_tilize_debug.py::test_r2_same_spec_is_zero_copy_not_merely_tolerated asserts cb.has_buffer() on BOTH CBs and resident==1 in both dataflow kernels. SECOND degree (fold the dataflow kernels away) deliberately NOT taken — examples/zero_copy_fold measured 0.74x at 2 tiles/core; it is Refinement 6's measurable step.

measured.note: Same arm as A2 (one edit, one off-arm). After the lever the resident path is COMPUTE-bound: ablate_compute alone drops sharded_big 2096 -> 403 ns (0.19x), which equals the ablate_all floor (421 ns) because there is no data-movement payload left to stub.

C15.followup: A3 makes the sharded path exist; after that this lever is the CALLER's choice of memory_config, not the op's. Nothing for the op to apply beyond supporting the layout natively.
C15.reason: The op does not choose its own tensor placement — memory_config is an argument. Predicted 0 for the interleaved cells this phase ships; the value of sharding shows up as C14 on cells that pass a sharded memory_config. Refinement 2 MEASURED the size of the caller-side choice this lever describes: the same [1,1,2048,2048] bf16 conversion is 44.1 us DRAM-interleaved and 2.09 us same-spec L1-sharded (21x) — the sharded call moves zero bytes. Still `deferred` and not `applied`, because the op cannot make that choice: memory_config is an argument.

C16.reason: Depth-2 CBs measure INSIDE the noise band against depth-1 in every regime, in BOTH phases that measured them. The ablation gives the mechanism on the DRAM shapes: compute is fully overlap-hidden (ablate_compute 0.994x on the square), so a deeper CB has nothing left to overlap. REFINEMENT 1 (A6): double_buffer=False is now IN SUPPORTED, so this is a user-facing L1-vs-perf knob, not just an internal lever - and the measurement says the L1 half is free: depth-1 HALVES per-core CB L1 (128 KiB -> 64 KiB at bf16 WT_BLOCK=16; 16 -> 8 KiB at WT_BLOCK=2) at a cost inside noise. Depth-2 stays the DEFAULT because use_double_buffer=True is the documented default of the public API. Re-measured this phase on all 6 bench shapes including the new l1_to_l1 direction, where the ablation profile is DIFFERENT (compute is co-binding at 0.596x, not hidden) and depth-1 still costs only 1.023x.

measured.note: Refinement 1 re-measure, per-regime off/on: square 0.998x, wide_short 1.009x, tall_narrow 1.001x, l1_to_l1[1,1,512,2048] 1.023x, smallest[1,1,32,64] 1.021x, smallest[1,1,32,32] 1.019x. Every regime within or just outside the 2-3% noise band; the two smallest regimes are the ones where depth-1 costs the most, per master.md B0.

C17.reason: A layout conversion cannot be in-place: RM->TILE moves every byte, and the tilize LLK helper itself static_asserts input_dfb != output_dfb (tilize_helpers.inl:116). Pinned by asserting the two CB slots differ and that the output tensor is a different buffer from the input.

D18.followup: APPLIED IN CODE (TensorAccessorArgs appended LAST as compile-time args in both dataflow kernels) but UNMEASURED, because a device-kernel-duration bench structurally CANNOT see it — the lever moves address-gen code and program-cache behaviour, not kernel ns. To close it: add a runtime-accessor-args arm (TensorAccessorArgs(..., ArgConfig::Runtime) plus the <cta, crta> kernel form) and compare dispatch time, or diff ttnn.compute_program_descriptor_hash. Named as a BENCH gap, not as a win.
D18.reason: Predicted ~0 on device kernel time; the payoff is dispatch/program-cache, which tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/tilize/test_tilize.py::test_tilize_program_cache_hit exercises together with D19. OBSERVED: a probe (tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/tilize/probes/probe_002.py) shows num_program_cache_entries 1 -> 1 across two identical-spec calls with identity intact on both, so the CT/RT split does cache as intended — but that is a dispatch observation, not the ns counterfactual this status would need.

D19.followup: Same bench gap as D18. Runtime args are already only (buffer address, b0, nb) — every shape-derived quantity is compile-time — so a second call with the same spec reuses the program. Close it by asserting the cache hit in the bench rather than in kernel ns.
D19.reason: Applied in code, unmeasurable in device kernel duration by construction. Recorded as open rather than claimed as a measured win. OBSERVED: a probe (tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/tilize/probes/probe_002.py) shows num_program_cache_entries 1 -> 1 across two identical-spec calls with identity intact on both, so the CT/RT split does cache as intended — but that is a dispatch observation, not the ns counterfactual this status would need.

D20.followup: A3/A3b/A3c and T2 introduce genuinely different data paths (zero-copy shard alias, crossover, cross-spec reshard, face-walking retile reader); op_design.md 5.3 already pins the regime-selection function. Implement it as the factory selector then.
D20.reason: There is exactly ONE data path at Phase 0 (interleaved RM -> TILE), so there is nothing to select between. Predicted 0 now; the lever's value arrives with the sharded/retile regimes.

D21.followup: Check whether TensorAccessor already specializes pow2 page sizes (shifts, not multiplies) on this path; if not, measure an InterleavedAddrGenFast-style specialization on the square, where address-gen runs 128 reads/core.
D21.reason: Small by nature (address arithmetic, not bytes), and the square is DRAM-bandwidth-bound at 84% of peak, so saving reader instructions is unlikely to move the wall. Worth a number only if a reader-issue-bound regime appears.

E22.followup: Out of single-op scope by construction: Metal Trace + multi-CQ removes HOST dispatch, which device kernel duration does not measure. Revisit at model level.
E22.reason: The smallest regime shows the shape of the cost it targets (ablate_all is 0.32us of a 1.87us launch, 17%), so the lever is real at model level — but it is not this op's to apply.
